source.text: וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י מֵאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And mustered David the people who [were] with him, and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

en.L: And David mustered the people who [were] with him, and he set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.
en.B: David counted the troops who were with him and appointed commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them.
en.R: David gathered his soldiers and counted them. Then he chose commanders to lead them, some over units of a thousand men and some over units of a hundred.

es.L: Y David pasó revista al pueblo que [estaba] con él, y puso sobre ellos jefes de millares y jefes de centenas.
es.B: David contó la tropa que estaba con él y nombró jefes de millares y jefes de centenas para ponerlos al frente.
es.R: David reunió a sus soldados y los contó. Luego escogió jefes para dirigirlos, unos al mando de grupos de mil hombres y otros al mando de grupos de cien.

fr.L: Et David passa en revue le peuple qui [était] avec lui, et il établit sur eux des chefs de milliers et des chefs de centaines.
fr.B: David passa en revue la troupe qui était avec lui et plaça à sa tête des chefs de milliers et des chefs de centaines.
fr.R: David a rassemblé ses soldats et les a comptés. Puis il a choisi des chefs pour les commander, les uns sur des groupes de mille hommes, les autres sur des groupes de cent.

sw.L: Daudi akawahesabu watu [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, akaweka juu yao majemadari wa maelfu na majemadari wa mamia.
sw.B: Daudi aliwahesabu askari waliokuwa pamoja naye, akaweka juu yao makamanda wa maelfu na makamanda wa mamia.
sw.R: Daudi akawakusanya askari wake akawahesabu. Kisha akachagua makamanda wa kuwaongoza, wengine juu ya vikosi vya watu elfu moja na wengine juu ya vikosi vya watu mia moja.

vi.L: Đa-vít điểm duyệt dân đi theo mình, và lập trên họ các trưởng nghìn người và các trưởng trăm người.
vi.B: Đa-vít kiểm điểm quân lính đi theo mình và lập các trưởng nghìn người, trưởng trăm người chỉ huy họ.
vi.R: Đa-vít tập hợp quân lính của mình và đếm họ. Rồi vua chọn những người chỉ huy để dẫn họ, có người chỉ huy đơn vị một nghìn người, có người chỉ huy đơn vị một trăm người.

ko.L: 다윗이 자기와 함께 있는 백성을 점검하고, 그들 위에 천부장들과 백부장들을 세웠다.
ko.B: 다윗은 자기와 함께 있는 군대를 점검하고, 그들 위에 천부장과 백부장을 세웠다.
ko.R: 다윗은 군사들을 모아 수를 세었다. 그리고 그들을 이끌 지휘관들을 뽑았는데, 어떤 사람은 천 명을, 어떤 사람은 백 명을 맡게 했다.

decisions.choice: mustered: counted the men and organized them for battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to look over, count or call up. Here David reviews the men who had come to him at Mahanaim (17:24, 27) and puts them in order for the coming battle, as Saul did in 1 Samuel 11:8 and 15:4.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and of hundreds: officers over the army's larger and smaller units
decisions.reason: Israel's army was divided into units called thousands and hundreds, each with its own commander (Exodus 18:21; 1 Samuel 8:12; 22:7). The names are those of the units; a unit need not have held exactly that number of men.

decisions.choice: the people who were with him: the men who had fled with David and those who had joined him
decisions.reason: David had left Jerusalem with his household, his officials and his guard (15:16-18), and others had come to him since. Absalom now had the larger army of Israel (17:11, 24-26).

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

decisions.choice: some over units of a thousand men and some over units of a hundred
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that thousands and hundreds are the sizes of the army's units.

decisions.choice: el pueblo (L); la tropa (B); los soldados, el ejército (R)
decisions.reason: For the battle chapters of this block: the Hebrew 'the people' is the fighting men, so Literal keeps 'el pueblo' and Balanced and Readable say 'la tropa' and 'los soldados' or 'el ejército', as the English decision does.

decisions.choice: majemadari (L); makamanda (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note has "jemadari wa jeshi" (L) and "mkuu wa jeshi" (B, R) for the army commander; the officers over thousands and hundreds follow the same split, "majemadari" at Literal and the everyday "makamanda" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "dân" (L); "quân lính" (B); "quân lính", "binh sĩ" (R) where "the people" is an army
decisions.reason: As the English levels do: Literal keeps the Hebrew "people", Balanced and Readable name the troops; kept through these chapters.

source.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח דָּוִ֜ד אֶת־הָעָ֗ם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית בְּיַד־יוֹאָב֙ וְ֠הַשְּׁלִשִׁית בְּיַ֨ד אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־צְרוּיָה֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וְהַ֨שְּׁלִשִׁ֔ת בְּיַ֖ד אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֑יסוַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם יָצֹ֥א אֵצֵ֛א גַּם־אֲנִ֖י עִמָּכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent out David the people, the third in [the] hand of Joab, and the third in [the] hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and the third in [the] hand of Ittai the Gittite. And said the king to the people, Going out I will go out, also I, with you.

en.L: And David sent out the people, a third under the hand of Joab, and a third under the hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I also will surely go out with you."
en.B: Then David sent the troops out in three divisions: one under Joab's command, one under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and one under Ittai the Gittite. The king told the troops, "I am going out with you myself."
en.R: David sent the army out in three groups. Joab led one group. Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah led another. Ittai from Gath led the third. The king told the soldiers, "I am going to march out with you too."

es.L: Y David envió al pueblo, una tercera parte bajo el mando de Joab, y una tercera parte bajo el mando de Abisai hijo de Sarvia, hermano de Joab, y una tercera parte bajo el mando de Itai el geteo. Y el rey dijo al pueblo: «Ciertamente yo también saldré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.B: Luego David envió la tropa en tres divisiones: una al mando de Joab, otra al mando de Abisai hijo de Sarvia, hermano de Joab, y otra al mando de Itai el geteo. El rey le dijo a la tropa: «Yo mismo saldré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: David envió al ejército en tres grupos. Joab dirigía uno. Abisai hijo de Sarvia, el hermano de Joab, dirigía otro. Itai, el de Gat, dirigía el tercero. El rey les dijo a los soldados: «Yo también voy a salir con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».

fr.L: Et David envoya le peuple, un tiers sous la main de Joab, un tiers sous la main d’Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, frère de Joab, et un tiers sous la main d’Ittaï le Guittite. Et le roi dit au peuple : « Moi aussi, je sortirai certainement avec vous. »
fr.B: Puis David fit partir la troupe en trois corps : l’un sous le commandement de Joab, l’autre sous celui d’Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, frère de Joab, et le troisième sous celui d’Ittaï le Guittite. Le roi dit à la troupe : « Je sortirai moi-même avec vous. »
fr.R: David a envoyé l’armée en trois groupes. Joab commandait le premier. Le frère de Joab, Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, commandait le deuxième. Ittaï, l’homme de Gath, commandait le troisième. Le roi a dit aux soldats : « Moi aussi, je vais partir au combat avec vous. »

sw.L: Daudi akawatuma watu, theluthi chini ya mkono wa Yoabu, na theluthi chini ya mkono wa Abishai mwana wa Seruya, ndugu wa Yoabu, na theluthi chini ya mkono wa Itai Mgiti. Mfalme akawaambia watu, "Hakika mimi nami nitatoka pamoja nanyi."
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akawatuma askari katika vikosi vitatu: kimoja chini ya Yoabu, kimoja chini ya Abishai mwana wa Seruya, ndugu wa Yoabu, na kimoja chini ya Itai Mgiti. Mfalme akawaambia askari, "Mimi mwenyewe nitatoka pamoja nanyi."
sw.R: Daudi akalituma jeshi katika vikundi vitatu. Yoabu akaongoza kikundi kimoja. Ndugu yake Yoabu, Abishai mwana wa Seruya, akaongoza kingine. Itai wa Gathi akaongoza cha tatu. Mfalme akawaambia askari, "Mimi nami nitakwenda vitani pamoja nanyi."

vi.L: Đa-vít sai dân đi ra, một phần ba dưới tay Giô-áp, một phần ba dưới tay A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, em Giô-áp, và một phần ba dưới tay Y-tai người Gát. Vua nói với dân: "Chính ta cũng chắc chắn sẽ đi ra với các ngươi."
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít chia quân làm ba cánh mà sai đi: một cánh do Giô-áp chỉ huy, một cánh do A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, em Giô-áp, chỉ huy, và một cánh do Y-tai người Gát chỉ huy. Vua bảo quân lính: "Chính ta cũng sẽ ra trận với các ngươi."
vi.R: Đa-vít chia quân làm ba nhóm và sai họ đi. Giô-áp dẫn một nhóm. A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, em Giô-áp, dẫn một nhóm khác. Y-tai người thành Gát dẫn nhóm thứ ba. Vua nói với binh sĩ: "Ta cũng sẽ cùng các ngươi ra trận."

ko.L: 다윗이 백성을 내보냈는데, 삼분의 일은 요압의 손 아래에, 삼분의 일은 요압의 형제 스루야의 아들 아비새의 손 아래에, 삼분의 일은 가드 사람 잇대의 손 아래에 두었다. 왕이 백성에게 말했다. "나도 반드시 너희와 함께 나가겠다."
ko.B: 다윗은 군대를 세 부대로 나누어 내보냈다. 한 부대는 요압이 지휘하고, 한 부대는 요압의 형제 스루야의 아들 아비새가 지휘하고, 한 부대는 가드 사람 잇대가 지휘했다. 왕이 군대에게 말했다. "나도 너희와 함께 나가겠다."
ko.R: 다윗은 군대를 세 무리로 나누어 내보냈다. 한 무리는 요압이 이끌었다. 또 한 무리는 요압의 형제인 스루야의 아들 아비새가 이끌었다. 나머지 한 무리는 가드에서 온 잇대가 이끌었다. 왕이 군사들에게 말했다. "나도 너희와 함께 싸우러 나가겠다."

decisions.choice: in the hand of: under the command of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and control. A third of the army "in the hand of Joab" is the third he led.

decisions.choice: Ittai the Gittite: a man from the Philistine city of Gath who had joined David
decisions.reason: Ittai had come to David with six hundred men from Gath shortly before Absalom's revolt and had sworn to stay with him whatever happened (15:18-22). David now trusts this foreigner with a third of his army, next to his own nephews Joab and Abishai.

decisions.choice: I will surely go out, I also: a firm decision
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, and "I also" stresses the king himself. David means to lead his men in person, as a king was expected to do (1 Samuel 8:20).

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the army, the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

decisions.choice: Ittai from Gath
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the Gittite" as the man's home town.

decisions.choice: Abishai is "em Giô-áp"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say which brother is older; Joab is always named first and leads, so Abishai is taken as the younger.

decisions.choice: "요압의 형제" for Joab's brother Abishai
decisions.reason: Korean would normally say whether a brother is older or younger, but the order of Zeruiah's sons is not certain (1 Chronicles 2:16 names Abishai first), so the neutral "형제" is kept.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֗א כִּי֩ אִם־נֹ֨ס נָנ֜וּס לֹא־יָשִׂ֧ימוּ אֵלֵ֣ינוּ לֵ֗ב וְאִם־יָמֻ֤תוּ חֶצְיֵ֨נוּ֙ לֹֽא־יָשִׂ֤ימוּ אֵלֵ֨ינוּ֙ לֵ֔ב כִּֽי־עַתָּ֥ה כָמֹ֖נוּ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה אֲלָפִ֑ים וְעַתָּ֣ה ט֔וֹב כִּי־תִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֥נוּ מֵעִ֖יר לַעְזֽוֹר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said the people, Not you shall go out, for if fleeing we flee, not they will set to us heart, and if die half of us, not they will set to us heart; for now like us [are] ten thousand; and now [it is] better that you be for us from [the] city to help.

en.L: But the people said, "You shall not go out. For if we indeed flee, they will not set [their] heart on us; and if half of us die, they will not set [their] heart on us. For now [you are] like 10,000 of us. And now [it is] better that you be for us from the city to help."
en.B: But the troops said, "You must not go out. If we have to run, they will not care about us. Even if half of us die, they will not care about us. But you are worth 10,000 of us. So it is better for you to help us from the city."
en.R: But the soldiers said, "You must not go out to fight. If we have to run away, the enemy will not care about us. Even if half of us are killed, they will not care. You are the one they want. You are worth 10,000 of us! So it is better for you to stay in the city and be ready to help us from there."

es.L: Pero el pueblo dijo: «No saldrás. Porque si de veras huimos, no pondrán en nosotros [su] corazón; y si muere la mitad de nosotros, no pondrán en nosotros [su] corazón. Porque ahora [tú eres] como diez mil de nosotros. Y ahora [es] mejor que tú nos sirvas de ayuda desde la ciudad».
es.B: Pero la tropa le dijo: «No debes salir. Si tenemos que huir, no les importaremos. Aunque muera la mitad de nosotros, no les importaremos. Pero tú vales por diez mil de nosotros. Así que es mejor que nos ayudes desde la ciudad».
es.R: Pero los soldados le dijeron: «No debes salir a pelear. Si tenemos que huir, al enemigo no le importaremos. Aunque maten a la mitad de nosotros, no les importará. Tú eres al que buscan. ¡Tú vales por diez mil de nosotros! Así que es mejor que te quedes en la ciudad, listo para ayudarnos desde allí».

fr.L: Mais le peuple dit : « Tu ne sortiras pas. Car si vraiment nous fuyons, ils ne mettront pas [leur] cœur sur nous ; et si la moitié d’entre nous meurt, ils ne mettront pas [leur] cœur sur nous. Car maintenant [tu es] comme dix mille d’entre nous. Et maintenant, [il est] mieux que tu sois pour nous, depuis la ville, une aide. »
fr.B: Mais la troupe répondit : « Tu ne dois pas sortir. Si nous devons fuir, ils ne s’occuperont pas de nous. Même si la moitié d’entre nous meurt, ils ne s’en soucieront pas. Mais toi, tu vaux dix mille d’entre nous. Il vaut donc mieux que tu nous viennes en aide depuis la ville. »
fr.R: Mais les soldats ont dit : « Tu ne dois pas partir au combat. Si nous devons nous enfuir, l’ennemi ne s’occupera pas de nous. Même si la moitié d’entre nous sont tués, cela lui sera égal. C’est toi qu’ils veulent. Tu vaux dix mille d’entre nous ! Il vaut donc mieux que tu restes dans la ville, prêt à nous aider de là-bas. »

sw.L: Lakini watu wakasema, "Usitoke. Kwa maana tukikimbia kweli, hawataweka moyo [wao] kwetu; na nusu yetu wakifa, hawataweka moyo [wao] kwetu. Kwa maana sasa [wewe ni] kama elfu kumi kati yetu. Basi sasa [ni] afadhali utusaidie kutoka mjini."
sw.B: Lakini askari wakasema, "Hupaswi kutoka. Ikiwa tutalazimika kukimbia, hawatatujali. Hata nusu yetu wakifa, hawatatujali. Lakini wewe una thamani ya watu elfu kumi kati yetu. Kwa hiyo ni afadhali utusaidie ukiwa mjini."
sw.R: Lakini askari wakasema, "Usiende vitani. Ikiwa tutalazimika kukimbia, adui hawatatujali. Hata nusu yetu wakiuawa, hawatajali. Wewe ndiye wanayekutaka. Una thamani ya watu elfu kumi kati yetu! Kwa hiyo ni afadhali ukae mjini, uwe tayari kutusaidia ukiwa huko."

vi.L: Nhưng dân nói: "Vua không được ra đi. Vì nếu chúng tôi phải chạy trốn, họ sẽ không để lòng đến chúng tôi; dù một nửa chúng tôi chết, họ cũng không để lòng đến chúng tôi. Nhưng bây giờ [vua] như 10.000 người chúng tôi. Vậy bây giờ tốt hơn là vua ở trong thành mà giúp chúng tôi."
vi.B: Nhưng quân lính thưa: "Bệ hạ không được ra trận. Nếu chúng tôi phải chạy trốn, họ cũng chẳng bận tâm đến chúng tôi. Dù một nửa chúng tôi có chết, họ cũng chẳng bận tâm. Nhưng bệ hạ đáng giá bằng 10.000 người chúng tôi. Vậy tốt hơn bệ hạ nên ở trong thành mà tiếp ứng cho chúng tôi."
vi.R: Nhưng binh sĩ thưa: "Đức vua không nên ra trận. Nếu chúng tôi phải chạy trốn, quân địch cũng chẳng quan tâm. Dù một nửa chúng tôi bị giết, chúng cũng chẳng quan tâm. Đức vua mới là người chúng muốn bắt. Đức vua đáng giá bằng 10.000 người chúng tôi! Vậy tốt hơn đức vua nên ở lại trong thành và sẵn sàng giúp chúng tôi từ đó."

ko.L: 그러나 백성이 말했다. "임금님은 나가시면 안 됩니다. 우리가 도망하더라도 그들은 우리에게 마음을 두지 않을 것이고, 우리 가운데 절반이 죽더라도 그들은 우리에게 마음을 두지 않을 것입니다. 이제 임금님은 우리 만 명과 같습니다. 그러니 이제 임금님께서는 성에서 우리를 도우시는 것이 더 좋겠습니다."
ko.B: 그러나 군사들이 말했다. "임금님께서는 나가시면 안 됩니다. 우리가 도망치게 되더라도 그들은 우리에게 관심을 두지 않을 것입니다. 우리 가운데 절반이 죽더라도 그들은 신경 쓰지 않을 것입니다. 그러나 임금님은 우리 만 명만큼 귀하십니다. 그러니 임금님께서는 성에서 우리를 도와주시는 것이 더 낫습니다."
ko.R: 그러나 군사들이 말했다. "임금님께서는 싸우러 나가시면 안 됩니다. 우리가 도망치게 되더라도 적들은 우리에게 관심이 없을 것입니다. 우리 가운데 절반이 죽더라도 신경 쓰지 않을 것입니다. 적들이 노리는 사람은 임금님이십니다. 임금님은 우리 만 명만큼 귀하십니다! 그러니 임금님께서는 성에 남아 계시다가 거기에서 우리를 도와주시는 것이 더 좋겠습니다."

decisions.choice: you are worth ten thousand of us
alternatives: for now there are ten thousand like us
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as its vowels read it has "for now like us ten thousand". The Greek and Latin translations and a few Hebrew manuscripts read the same consonants as "you" instead of "now": "for you are like ten thousand of us". The Hebrew text can give the same sense if "you are" is understood, and the next words ("it is better that you ...") show that the soldiers are speaking about the king. Read the other way, the Hebrew would mean "there are ten thousand like us", that is, the rest of the army can be spared but the king cannot. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: they will not set their heart on us: the enemy will not care about us
decisions.reason: To set the heart on something is to pay attention to it. Absalom's men will not care how many of David's soldiers run or die, because their target is the king himself, as Ahithophel had advised (17:2).

decisions.choice: help us from the city: support the battle from Mahanaim
decisions.reason: The king would stay safe in the city and could send help or receive the army if it had to fall back.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

decisions.choice: the enemy; You are the one they want
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are and states what the soldiers imply: Absalom's men are after the king (17:2).

decisions.choice: "dix mille" in words
decisions.reason: The French style guide writes numbers in words in running text; "dix mille" reads naturally at every level, where the English writes the figure.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־יִיטַ֥ב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם אֶעֱשֶׂ֑ה וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־יַ֣ד הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְכָל־הָעָם֙ יָֽצְא֔וּ לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the king, What is good in your eyes I will do. And stood the king at [the] side of the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

en.L: And the king said to them, "Whatever is good in your eyes I will do." And the king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
en.B: The king answered them, "I will do whatever you think best." So the king stood beside the gate while all the troops marched out in units of hundreds and of thousands.
en.R: The king told them, "I will do what you think is best." So he stood beside the city gate while the whole army marched out in groups of a hundred and of a thousand.

es.L: Y el rey les dijo: «Haré lo que sea bueno a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos». Y el rey se puso junto a la puerta, y todo el pueblo salió por centenas y por millares.
es.B: El rey les respondió: «Haré lo que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:les|os}} parezca mejor». Así que el rey se puso junto a la puerta mientras toda la tropa salía en grupos de cien y de mil.
es.R: El rey les dijo: «Haré lo que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:crean|creáis}} que es mejor». Así que se puso junto a la puerta de la ciudad mientras todo el ejército salía en grupos de cien y de mil.

fr.L: Et le roi leur dit : « Ce qui est bon à vos yeux, je le ferai. » Et le roi se tint à côté de la porte, et tout le peuple sortit par centaines et par milliers.
fr.B: Le roi leur répondit : « Je ferai ce que vous jugerez bon. » Le roi se tint donc à côté de la porte, pendant que toute la troupe sortait par centaines et par milliers.
fr.R: Le roi leur a dit : « Je ferai ce que vous pensez être le mieux. » Il s’est donc tenu à côté de la porte de la ville pendant que toute l’armée sortait par groupes de cent et de mille.

sw.L: Mfalme akawaambia, "Lolote lililo jema machoni penu nitalifanya." Mfalme akasimama kando ya lango, na watu wote wakatoka kwa mamia na kwa maelfu.
sw.B: Mfalme akawajibu, "Nitafanya lolote mnaloona ni bora." Basi mfalme akasimama kando ya lango wakati askari wote walipokuwa wakitoka kwa vikosi vya mamia na vya maelfu.
sw.R: Mfalme akawaambia, "Nitafanya mnavyoona ni bora." Basi akasimama kando ya lango la mji wakati jeshi lote lilipokuwa likitoka kwa vikundi vya watu mia moja na vya elfu moja.

vi.L: Vua nói với họ: "Điều gì tốt trong mắt các ngươi, ta sẽ làm." Vua đứng bên cổng thành, và toàn dân đi ra từng trăm từng nghìn.
vi.B: Vua đáp: "Các ngươi thấy thế nào là tốt, ta sẽ làm theo." Vậy vua đứng bên cổng thành, trong khi toàn quân kéo ra theo từng đơn vị trăm người và nghìn người.
vi.R: Vua nói với họ: "Ta sẽ làm theo điều các ngươi thấy là tốt nhất." Vậy vua đứng bên cổng thành trong khi cả đạo quân kéo ra theo từng nhóm một trăm và một nghìn người.

ko.L: 왕이 그들에게 말했다. "너희 눈에 좋은 대로 내가 하겠다." 왕은 성문 곁에 서 있고, 온 백성은 백 명씩, 천 명씩 나갔다.
ko.B: 왕이 그들에게 대답했다. "너희가 좋다고 생각하는 대로 하겠다." 그래서 왕은 성문 곁에 서 있었고, 온 군대는 백 명씩, 천 명씩 부대를 지어 나아갔다.
ko.R: 왕이 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 가장 좋다고 생각하는 대로 하겠다." 그래서 왕은 성문 곁에 섰고, 온 군대가 백 명씩, 천 명씩 무리를 지어 행진해 나갔다.

decisions.choice: good in your eyes: what you think best
decisions.reason: "In your eyes" means in your judgment. The king gives way to his men.

decisions.choice: the king stood beside the gate: watching his army march out
decisions.reason: The king took his place at the city gate as the units passed him, the last time he would see them before the battle. It is also where the men hear his order about Absalom (verse 5), and where he waits for news (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the whole army (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־י֠וֹאָב וְאֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְאַט־לִ֖י לַנַּ֣עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וְכָל־הָעָ֣ם שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּצַוֺּ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־כָּל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים עַל־דְּבַ֥ר אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Gently for me with the young man, with Absalom. And all the people heard when commanded the king all the commanders concerning [the] matter of Absalom.

en.L: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, "[Deal] gently for my sake with the young man, with Absalom." And all the people heard when the king commanded all the commanders concerning the matter of Absalom.
en.B: The king gave an order to Joab, Abishai and Ittai: "For my sake, deal gently with the young man Absalom." All the troops heard the king give this order about Absalom to all the commanders.
en.R: The king gave orders to Joab, Abishai and Ittai. He said, "For my sake, be gentle with young Absalom." All the soldiers heard the king give all the commanders this order about Absalom.

es.L: Y el rey ordenó a Joab, a Abisai y a Itai, diciendo: «[{{plural_you:Traten|Tratad}}] con suavidad, por amor a mí, al joven, a Absalón». Y todo el pueblo oyó cuando el rey dio órdenes a todos los jefes acerca de Absalón.
es.B: El rey dio una orden a Joab, a Abisai y a Itai: «Por amor a mí, {{plural_you:traten|tratad}} con suavidad al joven Absalón». Toda la tropa oyó al rey dar esta orden acerca de Absalón a todos los jefes.
es.R: El rey dio órdenes a Joab, a Abisai y a Itai. Les dijo: «Por amor a mí, no le {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} daño al joven Absalón». Todos los soldados oyeron al rey dar a todos los jefes esta orden acerca de Absalón.

fr.L: Et le roi commanda à Joab, à Abishaï et à Ittaï, disant : « Doucement, pour moi, avec le jeune homme, avec Absalom ! » Et tout le peuple entendit quand le roi donna ses ordres à tous les chefs au sujet d’Absalom.
fr.B: Le roi donna cet ordre à Joab, à Abishaï et à Ittaï : « Par égard pour moi, ménagez le jeune Absalom. » Toute la troupe entendit le roi donner cet ordre à tous les chefs au sujet d’Absalom.
fr.R: Le roi a donné des ordres à Joab, à Abishaï et à Ittaï. Il leur a dit : « Pour moi, soyez doux avec le jeune Absalom. » Tous les soldats ont entendu le roi donner cet ordre à tous les chefs au sujet d’Absalom.

sw.L: Mfalme akamwamuru Yoabu na Abishai na Itai, akisema, "[Mtendeeni] kwa upole kwa ajili yangu kijana, Absalomu." Na watu wote wakasikia mfalme alipowaamuru majemadari wote kuhusu jambo la Absalomu.
sw.B: Mfalme akawapa Yoabu, Abishai na Itai amri hii: "Kwa ajili yangu, mtendeeni kwa upole kijana Absalomu." Askari wote wakamsikia mfalme akiwapa makamanda wote amri hiyo kuhusu Absalomu.
sw.R: Mfalme akawapa Yoabu, Abishai na Itai amri. Akasema, "Kwa ajili yangu, mtendeeni kijana Absalomu kwa upole." Askari wote wakamsikia mfalme akiwapa makamanda wote amri hiyo kuhusu Absalomu.

vi.L: Vua truyền lệnh cho Giô-áp, A-bi-sai và Y-tai rằng: "Vì cớ ta, [hãy đối xử] nhẹ tay với chàng trai, với Áp-sa-lôm." Toàn dân đều nghe khi vua truyền lệnh cho tất cả các tướng về việc Áp-sa-lôm.
vi.B: Vua ra lệnh cho Giô-áp, A-bi-sai và Y-tai: "Vì ta, hãy nương tay với chàng trai Áp-sa-lôm." Toàn quân đều nghe vua truyền lệnh ấy về Áp-sa-lôm cho tất cả các tướng.
vi.R: Vua ra lệnh cho Giô-áp, A-bi-sai và Y-tai. Vua nói: "Vì ta, hãy nương tay với Áp-sa-lôm trẻ tuổi." Tất cả binh sĩ đều nghe vua ra lệnh này cho các tướng về Áp-sa-lôm.

ko.L: 왕이 요압과 아비새와 잇대에게 명령하여 말했다. "나를 위해 그 젊은이, 압살롬을 너그럽게 [대하여라]." 왕이 압살롬의 일에 대해 모든 지휘관에게 명령할 때 온 백성이 들었다.
ko.B: 왕은 요압과 아비새와 잇대에게 명령했다. "나를 보아서라도 젊은 압살롬을 너그럽게 대하여라." 왕이 압살롬에 대하여 모든 지휘관에게 이렇게 명령하는 것을 온 군대가 들었다.
ko.R: 왕은 요압과 아비새와 잇대에게 명령을 내렸다. 왕이 말했다. "나를 보아서 젊은 압살롬을 부드럽게 대하여라." 왕이 모든 지휘관에게 압살롬에 대해 이렇게 명령하는 것을 모든 군사가 들었다.

decisions.choice: gently for me: go easy on him, for my sake
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and urgent: "gently, for me". David asks his commanders to spare Absalom because of what Absalom means to him, not because Absalom deserves it.

decisions.choice: the young man: said with a father's affection
decisions.reason: The word can mean a boy, a young man or a servant. Absalom was a grown man with children (14:27) and was leading a revolt, but David speaks of him as "the young man", as if he were still a youth who could be forgiven. The word comes back in verses 12, 29 and 32.

decisions.choice: all the people heard: the whole army knew the order
decisions.reason: The narrator makes sure that no one could later claim not to know what the king wanted; the soldier in verse 12 says the same.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֛ם הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִקְרַ֣את יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בְּיַ֥עַר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the people [to] the field to meet Israel, and was the battle in [the] forest of Ephraim.

en.L: And the people went out into the field to meet Israel, and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
en.B: The army marched out into the open country to face Israel, and the battle was fought in the forest of Ephraim.
en.R: So David's army went out into the countryside to fight the army of Israel. The battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

es.L: Y el pueblo salió al campo al encuentro de Israel, y la batalla fue en el bosque de Efraín.
es.B: El ejército salió a campo abierto para enfrentarse a Israel, y la batalla se libró en el bosque de Efraín.
es.R: Así que el ejército de David salió al campo para pelear contra el ejército de Israel. La batalla tuvo lugar en el bosque de Efraín.

fr.L: Et le peuple sortit dans la campagne à la rencontre d’Israël, et la bataille eut lieu dans la forêt d’Éphraïm.
fr.B: L’armée sortit en rase campagne pour affronter Israël, et la bataille se livra dans la forêt d’Éphraïm.
fr.R: L’armée de David est donc sortie dans la campagne pour combattre l’armée d’Israël. La bataille a eu lieu dans la forêt d’Éphraïm.

sw.L: Watu wakatoka kwenda uwanjani kukutana na Israeli, na vita vikawa katika msitu wa Efraimu.
sw.B: Jeshi likatoka kwenda nchi wazi kupambana na Israeli, na vita vikapiganwa katika msitu wa Efraimu.
sw.R: Basi jeshi la Daudi likatoka kwenda mashambani kupigana na jeshi la Israeli. Vita vikapiganwa katika msitu wa Efraimu.

vi.L: Dân đi ra đồng để đón đánh Y-sơ-ra-ên, và trận chiến diễn ra trong rừng Ép-ra-im.
vi.B: Quân đội kéo ra đồng trống để đối đầu với Y-sơ-ra-ên, và trận chiến diễn ra trong rừng Ép-ra-im.
vi.R: Vậy quân của Đa-vít kéo ra vùng quê để đánh quân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Trận chiến diễn ra trong rừng Ép-ra-im.

ko.L: 백성이 이스라엘을 맞으러 들로 나갔고, 에브라임 숲에서 싸움이 벌어졌다.
ko.B: 군대가 이스라엘과 맞서려고 들로 나갔고, 에브라임 숲에서 싸움이 벌어졌다.
ko.R: 다윗의 군대는 이스라엘 군대와 싸우려고 들판으로 나갔다. 싸움은 에브라임 숲에서 벌어졌다.

decisions.choice: Israel: the Israelites who had followed Absalom
decisions.reason: "Israel" here is Absalom's army, drawn from the tribes who had turned to him (15:13; 17:11, 24-26), set against David's own men.

decisions.choice: the forest of Ephraim: a wooded region east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The battle was fought near Mahanaim in Gilead (17:24, 26), east of the Jordan, not in the tribal land of Ephraim west of the river. Why the woods there carried Ephraim's name is not known.

decisions.choice: to meet: to meet in battle
decisions.reason: The verb "meet" often means going out against an enemy (1 Samuel 4:1; 17:48).

decisions.choice: the army (Balanced); David's army (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers". Readable names David to make clear which army is meant.

source.text: וַיִּנָּ֤גְפוּ שָׁם֙ עַ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַתְּהִי־שָׁ֞ם הַמַּגֵּפָ֧ה גְדוֹלָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And were defeated there [the] people of Israel before [the] servants of David, and was there the slaughter great on that day, twenty thousand.

en.L: And the people of Israel were struck down there before the servants of David, and the slaughter there was great on that day: 20,000.
en.B: There the army of Israel was defeated by David's men, and the slaughter there that day was great: 20,000 men.
en.R: David's men beat the army of Israel there. Many men were killed that day: 20,000 of them.

es.L: Y el pueblo de Israel fue derrotado allí delante de los siervos de David, y hubo allí aquel día una gran matanza: veinte mil.
es.B: Allí el ejército de Israel fue derrotado por los hombres de David, y aquel día hubo una gran matanza: veinte mil hombres.
es.R: Los hombres de David derrotaron allí al ejército de Israel. Ese día murieron muchos hombres: veinte mil.

fr.L: Et le peuple d’Israël fut battu là devant les serviteurs de David, et le massacre fut grand là, en ce jour-là : vingt mille.
fr.B: Là, l’armée d’Israël fut battue par les hommes de David, et le massacre fut grand ce jour-là : vingt mille hommes.
fr.R: Les hommes de David ont battu l’armée d’Israël à cet endroit. Beaucoup d’hommes ont été tués ce jour-là : vingt mille.

sw.L: Watu wa Israeli wakapigwa huko mbele ya watumishi wa Daudi, na machinjo yalikuwa makubwa huko siku ile: elfu ishirini.
sw.B: Huko jeshi la Israeli lilishindwa na watu wa Daudi, na mauaji yalikuwa makubwa siku ile: watu elfu ishirini.
sw.R: Watu wa Daudi wakalishinda jeshi la Israeli huko. Watu wengi waliuawa siku ile: watu elfu ishirini.

vi.L: Tại đó dân Y-sơ-ra-ên bị đánh bại trước các đầy tớ của Đa-vít, và cuộc tàn sát tại đó trong ngày ấy thật lớn: 20.000 [người].
vi.B: Tại đó quân Y-sơ-ra-ên bị người của Đa-vít đánh bại, và ngày ấy số người bị giết rất lớn: 20.000 người.
vi.R: Người của Đa-vít đánh bại quân Y-sơ-ra-ên tại đó. Ngày hôm ấy rất nhiều người bị giết: 20.000 người.

ko.L: 거기에서 이스라엘 백성이 다윗의 신하들 앞에서 패했고, 그날 그곳의 살육은 커서 이만 명에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 거기에서 이스라엘 군대가 다윗의 부하들에게 패했다. 그날 그곳에서 큰 살육이 벌어져 이만 명이 죽었다.
ko.R: 다윗의 부하들이 그곳에서 이스라엘 군대를 무찔렀다. 그날 많은 사람이 죽었는데, 그 수가 이만 명이나 되었다.

decisions.choice: the servants of David: the soldiers loyal to David
decisions.reason: "Servants" here are the men who serve the king as soldiers, as in 2:12-17.

decisions.choice: were struck down; the slaughter: a heavy defeat with many dead
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root, "strike". Israel was not only beaten but suffered great losses.

decisions.choice: David's men
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "servants"; Balanced and Readable say "men", since these are David's soldiers, not household servants.
The Hebrew gives only the number; Balanced and Readable add "men".

source.text: וַתְּהִי־שָׁ֧ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה נָפֹ֖צֶתעַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיֶּ֤רֶב הַיַּ֨עַר֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל בָּעָ֔ם מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָכְלָ֛ה הַחֶ֖רֶב בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And was there the battle spread over [the] face of all the land, and more [did] the forest to devour among the people than what devoured the sword on that day.

en.L: And the battle there was spread over the face of all the land, and the forest devoured more among the people than the sword devoured on that day.
en.B: The fighting spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest claimed more lives that day than the sword did.
en.R: The fighting spread all over the countryside. That day the forest killed more men than the swords did.

es.L: Y la batalla se extendió allí por la faz de toda la tierra, y el bosque devoró aquel día más gente que la que devoró la espada.
es.B: La lucha se extendió por toda la región, y aquel día el bosque se cobró más vidas que la espada.
es.R: La lucha se extendió por toda la región. Ese día el bosque mató a más hombres que las espadas.

fr.L: Et la bataille se répandit là sur la face de tout le pays, et la forêt dévora parmi le peuple plus que n’en dévora l’épée, en ce jour-là.
fr.B: Le combat s’étendit à toute la région, et la forêt fit ce jour-là plus de victimes que l’épée.
fr.R: Le combat s’est répandu dans toute la campagne. Ce jour-là, la forêt a tué plus d’hommes que les épées.

sw.L: Vita vikaenea huko juu ya uso wa nchi yote, na msitu ukala watu wengi zaidi kuliko upanga ulivyokula siku ile.
sw.B: Mapigano yakaenea katika nchi yote, na msitu ukaua watu wengi siku ile kuliko upanga.
sw.R: Mapigano yakaenea kila mahali mashambani. Siku ile msitu uliua watu wengi kuliko panga zilivyoua.

vi.L: Trận chiến lan rộng ra khắp mặt đất vùng ấy, và trong ngày ấy rừng nuốt nhiều người hơn gươm đã nuốt.
vi.B: Trận chiến lan ra khắp vùng, và ngày hôm ấy rừng cướp đi nhiều mạng người hơn cả gươm giáo.
vi.R: Trận đánh lan ra khắp vùng quê. Ngày hôm ấy số người chết trong rừng còn nhiều hơn số người chết vì gươm.

ko.L: 싸움이 거기에서 온 땅 위로 퍼졌는데, 그날 숲이 삼킨 백성이 칼이 삼킨 것보다 더 많았다.
ko.B: 싸움은 온 지역으로 퍼졌다. 그날 숲에서 목숨을 잃은 사람이 칼에 죽은 사람보다 더 많았다.
ko.R: 싸움은 온 들판으로 번졌다. 그날 칼에 죽은 사람보다 숲에서 죽은 사람이 더 많았다.

decisions.choice: the forest devoured more than the sword: more died in the forest than in the fighting
decisions.reason: Swords "devour" in Hebrew idiom (2:26; 11:25). Here the forest itself is said to devour: men fleeing through thick woods, rough ground and pits died there in greater numbers than in combat. The text does not say how; Absalom's own end (verses 9 and 17) shows the forest at work.

decisions.choice: all the land: the whole area of the battle
decisions.reason: The word can mean a country or a stretch of ground. Here it is the region around the forest, not all Israel.

decisions.choice: claimed more lives
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the forest as a killer without the word "devour".

source.text: וַיִּקָּרֵא֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְאַבְשָׁל֞וֹם רֹכֵ֣ב עַל־הַפֶּ֗רֶד וַיָּבֹ֣א הַפֶּ֡רֶד תַּ֣חַת שׂוֹבֶךְ֩ הָאֵלָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה וַיֶּחֱזַ֧ק רֹאשׁ֣וֹ בָאֵלָ֗ה וַיֻּתַּן֙ בֵּ֤ין הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהַפֶּ֥רֶד אֲשֶׁר־תַּחְתָּ֖יו עָבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And happened to meet Absalom before [the] servants of David, and Absalom [was] riding on the mule, and went the mule under [the] thick branches of the terebinth, the great [one], and held fast his head in the terebinth, and he was put between the heavens and between the earth, and the mule that [was] under him passed on.

en.L: And Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. And Absalom [was] riding on the mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great terebinth, and his head caught fast in the terebinth, and he was left between the heavens and the earth, and the mule that [was] under him passed on.
en.B: Absalom happened to come upon some of David's men. He was riding his mule, and when it passed beneath the tangled branches of a great terebinth, Absalom's head was caught fast in the tree. He was left hanging between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him kept going.
en.R: Absalom happened to run into some of David's men. He was riding on his mule. The mule went under the thick branches of a big tree, and Absalom's head got stuck in the branches. He was left hanging in the air, and the mule ran on without him.

es.L: Y Absalón se encontró con los siervos de David. Y Absalón [iba] montado en el mulo, y el mulo entró por debajo de las ramas espesas de la gran encina, y se le enredó la cabeza en la encina, y quedó suspendido entre el cielo y la tierra, y el mulo que [estaba] debajo de él siguió adelante.
es.B: Absalón se topó con algunos de los hombres de David. Iba montado en su mulo, y cuando el mulo pasó por debajo de las ramas enmarañadas de una gran encina, a Absalón se le quedó atrapada la cabeza en el árbol. Quedó colgando entre el cielo y la tierra, mientras el mulo que montaba seguía de largo.
es.R: Absalón se encontró de pronto con algunos de los hombres de David. Iba montado en su mulo. El mulo pasó por debajo de las ramas espesas de un árbol grande, y la cabeza de Absalón se quedó atrapada en las ramas. Se quedó colgando en el aire, y el mulo siguió corriendo sin él.

fr.L: Et Absalom se trouva en face des serviteurs de David. Et Absalom [était] monté sur le mulet, et le mulet passa sous les branches touffues du grand térébinthe, et sa tête s’accrocha au térébinthe, et il resta entre le ciel et la terre, et le mulet qui [était] sous lui passa outre.
fr.B: Absalom se trouva par hasard face à des hommes de David. Il était monté sur son mulet, et quand celui-ci passa sous les branches entremêlées d’un grand térébinthe, la tête d’Absalom resta prise dans l’arbre. Il demeura suspendu entre le ciel et la terre, tandis que le mulet qui le portait continuait sa course.
fr.R: Absalom est tombé par hasard sur des hommes de David. Il était sur son mulet. Le mulet est passé sous les branches épaisses d’un grand arbre, et la tête d’Absalom s’est coincée dans les branches. Il est resté pendu en l’air, et le mulet a continué sans lui.

sw.L: Absalomu akakutana na watumishi wa Daudi kwa bahati. Absalomu [alikuwa] amepanda nyumbu wake, na nyumbu akapita chini ya matawi manene ya mwaloni mkubwa, na kichwa chake kikanaswa katika mwaloni, naye akaachwa kati ya mbingu na nchi, na nyumbu aliyekuwa chini yake akaendelea.
sw.B: Absalomu akakutana kwa ghafla na baadhi ya watu wa Daudi. Alikuwa amepanda nyumbu wake, na nyumbu alipopita chini ya matawi yaliyosongamana ya mwaloni mkubwa, kichwa cha Absalomu kikanaswa kwa nguvu katika mti huo. Akabaki ananing'inia kati ya mbingu na nchi, huku nyumbu aliyekuwa chini yake akiendelea na safari.
sw.R: Absalomu akakutana kwa bahati na baadhi ya watu wa Daudi. Alikuwa amepanda nyumbu wake. Nyumbu akapita chini ya matawi manene ya mti mkubwa, na kichwa cha Absalomu kikakwama katika matawi. Akabaki ananing'inia hewani, na nyumbu akaendelea kukimbia bila yeye.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm tình cờ gặp các đầy tớ của Đa-vít. Áp-sa-lôm [đang] cưỡi la, và con la đi dưới những nhánh rậm của cây sồi lớn; đầu chàng mắc chặt vào cây sồi, và chàng bị treo lơ lửng giữa trời và đất, còn con la dưới chàng thì cứ đi.
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm tình cờ chạm trán một số người của Đa-vít. Chàng đang cưỡi la, và khi con la chạy dưới những cành rậm rạp của một cây sồi lớn, đầu chàng bị mắc chặt vào cây. Chàng bị treo lơ lửng giữa trời và đất, còn con la chàng đang cưỡi cứ thế chạy đi.
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm tình cờ gặp một số người của Đa-vít. Chàng đang cưỡi la. Con la chạy dưới những cành rậm của một cái cây lớn, và đầu Áp-sa-lôm bị mắc vào cành cây. Chàng bị treo lơ lửng trên không, còn con la thì chạy mất.

ko.L: 압살롬이 우연히 다윗의 신하들과 마주쳤다. 압살롬은 노새를 타고 있었는데, 노새가 큰 테레빈나무의 빽빽한 가지 아래로 지나가다가 그의 머리가 테레빈나무에 걸렸다. 그래서 그는 하늘과 땅 사이에 매달렸고, 그가 타고 있던 노새는 지나가 버렸다.
ko.B: 압살롬은 우연히 다윗의 부하들과 마주쳤다. 그는 노새를 타고 있었는데, 노새가 큰 테레빈나무의 얽힌 가지 아래로 지나갈 때 압살롬의 머리가 그 나무에 꽉 걸리고 말았다. 그는 하늘과 땅 사이에 매달렸고, 그가 타고 있던 노새는 그대로 달려가 버렸다.
ko.R: 압살롬은 우연히 다윗의 부하들과 마주쳤다. 그는 노새를 타고 있었다. 노새가 큰 나무의 빽빽한 가지 아래로 지나가는데, 압살롬의 머리가 나뭇가지에 걸렸다. 압살롬은 공중에 매달렸고, 노새는 압살롬을 두고 계속 달려가 버렸다.

decisions.choice: happened to meet: came upon them by chance
decisions.reason: The verb form describes an encounter that was not planned. Absalom, fleeing or riding through the forest, suddenly finds himself in front of David's soldiers.

decisions.choice: the mule: the mount of the king's sons
decisions.reason: Mules were ridden by David's sons (13:29), and David has Solomon ride his own mule at his crowning (1 Kings 1:33). Absalom rides as a prince, and the mule going on without him is a picture of his kingship leaving him.

decisions.choice: his head caught fast: his head was wedged in the branches
alternatives: his hair caught in the tree
decisions.reason: The text says that his head was caught. Absalom's thick hair has been mentioned (14:26), and many readers have pictured him caught by it, but this verse does not say so.

decisions.choice: between the heavens and the earth: hanging in midair
decisions.reason: The phrase describes something hanging above the ground with nothing below it (compare 1 Chronicles 21:16). Absalom hangs helpless, neither riding nor standing.

decisions.choice: the terebinth: a large, spreading tree
decisions.reason: The word names a big tree, the terebinth or a kind of oak, as in Judges 6:11.

decisions.choice: a big tree; hanging in the air
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the terebinth and for "between the heavens and the earth".

decisions.choice: David's men
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: la encina (L, B); un árbol grande (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tree is a terebinth or a large oak; Spanish 'encina' names a large, spreading tree that readers know, where 'terebinto' would be unfamiliar. Readable says only 'un árbol grande', as the English 'a big tree'.

decisions.choice: mwaloni (L, B); mti mkubwa (R)
decisions.reason: The terebinth is a large spreading tree (meaning decision m5) with no everyday Swahili name; "mwaloni", the usual Swahili word for the oak and its kin, stands for it, and Readable says only "a big tree", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "cây sồi" (L, B); "cái cây lớn" (R) for the terebinth
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no common name for the terebinth; "cây sồi" names a big spreading tree readers know, and Readable says only "a big tree", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "테레빈나무" (L, B); "큰 나무" (R)
decisions.reason: The *elah* is the terebinth, a large spreading tree of the hills, as the English has it; "상수리나무" (oak) is the older Korean rendering. Readable says only "a big tree", as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם תָּל֖וּי בָּאֵלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw a man, one, and told Joab, and said, Look, I saw Absalom hanging in the terebinth.

en.L: And a certain man saw [it] and told Joab, and he said, "Look, I saw Absalom hanging in the terebinth."
en.B: One man saw it and told Joab, "I have just seen Absalom hanging in a terebinth!"
en.R: One of the soldiers saw this and told Joab, "I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!"

es.L: Y un hombre [lo] vio y avisó a Joab, y dijo: «He aquí, vi a Absalón colgado de la encina».
es.B: Un hombre lo vio y se lo contó a Joab: «¡Acabo de ver a Absalón colgado de una encina!».
es.R: Uno de los soldados vio esto y le dijo a Joab: «¡Vi a Absalón colgado de un árbol!».

fr.L: Et un homme [le] vit et l’annonça à Joab, et dit : « Voici, j’ai vu Absalom suspendu dans le térébinthe. »
fr.B: Un homme le vit et vint dire à Joab : « Je viens de voir Absalom suspendu à un térébinthe ! »
fr.R: Un des soldats a vu cela et l’a dit à Joab : « J’ai vu Absalom pendu dans un arbre ! »

sw.L: Mtu mmoja akaona [hilo] akamwambia Yoabu, akasema, "Tazama, nimemwona Absalomu akining'inia katika mwaloni."
sw.B: Mtu mmoja akaona, akamwambia Yoabu, "Nimemwona Absalomu sasa hivi akining'inia katika mwaloni!"
sw.R: Askari mmoja akaona jambo hilo, akamwambia Yoabu, "Nimemwona Absalomu akining'inia mtini!"

vi.L: Có một người thấy [việc ấy] và báo cho Giô-áp rằng: "Kìa, tôi thấy Áp-sa-lôm bị treo trên cây sồi."
vi.B: Có một người thấy vậy liền báo cho Giô-áp: "Tôi vừa thấy Áp-sa-lôm bị treo trên một cây sồi!"
vi.R: Một người lính thấy vậy và báo cho Giô-áp: "Tôi thấy Áp-sa-lôm bị treo trên cây!"

ko.L: 어떤 사람이 [그것을] 보고 요압에게 알려 말했다. "보십시오, 제가 압살롬이 테레빈나무에 매달려 있는 것을 보았습니다."
ko.B: 한 사람이 그것을 보고 요압에게 알렸다. "압살롬이 테레빈나무에 매달려 있는 것을 방금 보았습니다!"
ko.R: 군사 한 사람이 그것을 보고 요압에게 알렸다. "압살롬이 나무에 매달려 있는 것을 보았습니다!"

decisions.choice: look: a word that calls attention to surprising news
decisions.reason: The man stresses what he has seen: the king's son, hanging helpless in a tree.

decisions.choice: One of the soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says that the man was one of David's soldiers, as verses 9 and 12 make clear.

decisions.choice: the soldier says "ông" and "tôi" to Joab; Joab says "ngươi" and "ta"
decisions.reason: A soldier to his commander and the commander to his soldier.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב לָאִישׁ֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ וְהִנֵּ֣ה רָאִ֔יתָ וּמַדּ֛וּעַ לֹֽא־הִכִּית֥וֹ שָׁ֖ם אָ֑רְצָה וְעָלַ֗י לָ֤תֶת לְךָ֙ עֲשָׂ֣רָה כֶ֔סֶף וַחֲגֹרָ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joab to the man who told him, And look, you saw, and why not did you strike him there to the ground? And on me [it would have been] to give to you ten [of] silver and one belt.

en.L: And Joab said to the man who told him, "And look, you saw [him]! Then why did you not strike him there to the ground? And it would have been on me to give you ten [shekels of] silver and a belt."
en.B: Joab said to the man who had told him, "You saw him? Then why did you not strike him down to the ground right there? I would have given you {{units:about 4 ounces of silver|ten shekels of silver}} and a belt."
en.R: Joab said to the man, "You saw him? Then why did you not kill him right there and let him fall to the ground? I would have given you {{units:about 4 ounces of silver|ten shekels of silver}} and a soldier's belt."

es.L: Y Joab dijo al hombre que le avisó: «¡Y he aquí, [lo] viste! ¿Por qué, pues, no lo heriste allí, [derribándolo] a tierra? Y a mí me habría tocado darte diez [siclos de] plata y un cinturón».
es.B: Joab le dijo al hombre que le había avisado: «¿Lo viste? ¿Y por qué no lo derribaste allí mismo al suelo? Yo te habría dado {{units:unos 115 gramos de plata|diez siclos de plata}} y un cinturón».
es.R: Joab le dijo al hombre: «¿Lo viste? ¿Y por qué no lo mataste allí mismo y lo dejaste caer al suelo? Yo te habría dado {{units:unos 115 gramos de plata|diez siclos de plata}} y un cinturón de soldado».

fr.L: Et Joab dit à l’homme qui le lui avait annoncé : « Et voici, tu [l’]as vu ! Pourquoi ne l’as-tu pas frappé là, à terre ? Et c’eût été à moi de te donner dix [sicles d’]argent et une ceinture. »
fr.B: Joab dit à l’homme qui l’avait informé : « Tu l’as vu ? Alors pourquoi ne l’as-tu pas abattu sur place ? Je t’aurais donné {{units:environ 115 grammes d’argent|dix sicles d’argent}} et une ceinture. »
fr.R: Joab a dit à l’homme : « Tu l’as vu ? Alors pourquoi ne l’as-tu pas tué tout de suite pour le faire tomber par terre ? Je t’aurais donné {{units:environ 115 grammes d’argent|dix sicles d’argent}} et une ceinture de soldat. »

sw.L: Yoabu akamwambia yule mtu aliyemwambia, "Na tazama, umemwona! Basi kwa nini hukumpiga huko hata chini? Ingekuwa juu yangu kukupa [shekeli] kumi za fedha na mshipi."
sw.B: Yoabu akamwambia yule mtu aliyempa habari, "Umemwona? Basi kwa nini hukumpiga akaanguka chini papo hapo? Ningekupa {{units:kama gramu 115 za fedha|shekeli kumi za fedha}} na mshipi."
sw.R: Yoabu akamwambia yule mtu, "Umemwona? Basi kwa nini hukumwua papo hapo akaanguka chini? Ningekupa {{units:kama gramu 115 za fedha|shekeli kumi za fedha}} na mshipi wa askari."

vi.L: Giô-áp nói với người báo tin: "Kìa, ngươi đã thấy [nó]! Vậy sao ngươi không đánh nó ngã xuống đất tại đó? Ta sẽ phải cho ngươi mười [siếc-lơ] bạc và một cái đai lưng."
vi.B: Giô-áp nói với người báo tin: "Ngươi đã thấy nó sao? Thế sao ngươi không đánh nó ngã xuống đất ngay tại chỗ? Ta đã thưởng cho ngươi {{units:khoảng 115 gam bạc|mười siếc-lơ bạc}} và một cái đai lưng rồi."
vi.R: Giô-áp nói với người ấy: "Ngươi đã thấy nó sao? Thế sao ngươi không giết nó ngay tại đó cho nó rơi xuống đất? Ta đã thưởng cho ngươi {{units:khoảng 115 gam bạc|mười siếc-lơ bạc}} và một cái đai lưng của chiến binh rồi."

ko.L: 요압이 자기에게 알린 사람에게 말했다. "보아라, 네가 [그를] 보았다면서, 어찌하여 거기에서 그를 쳐서 땅에 떨어뜨리지 않았느냐? 그랬으면 내가 너에게 은 열 [세겔]과 띠 하나를 주었을 것이다."
ko.B: 요압이 자기에게 알린 사람에게 말했다. "네가 그를 보았다고? 그런데 왜 그 자리에서 그를 쳐서 땅에 떨어뜨리지 않았느냐? 그랬으면 내가 너에게 {{units:은 115그램쯤|은 열 세겔}}과 띠 하나를 주었을 것이다."
ko.R: 요압이 그 사람에게 말했다. "네가 그를 보았다고? 그런데 왜 그 자리에서 그를 죽여 땅에 떨어뜨리지 않았느냐? 그랬으면 내가 너에게 {{units:은 115그램쯤|은 열 세겔}}과 군인의 띠 하나를 주었을 것이다."

decisions.choice: strike him to the ground: kill him
decisions.reason: To strike someone down "to the ground" is to kill him. Joab does not hide that he wanted Absalom dead, in spite of the king's order (verse 5).

decisions.choice: ten of silver: ten shekels of silver
decisions.reason: The unit is not named, but sums of silver were normally weighed in shekels. Ten shekels was a good reward for a soldier.

decisions.choice: a belt: a warrior's belt, given as an honor
decisions.reason: A belt held a soldier's sword and was a sign of rank; Jonathan gave David his belt with his armor (1 Samuel 18:4). Joab offers both money and honor.

decisions.choice: on me to give: it would have been my part to give
decisions.reason: Joab means that he would gladly have paid the reward himself.

decisions.choice: about 4 ounces of silver
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in modern terms, with the shekel as the alternative; Literal supplies the unit in brackets.

decisions.choice: kill him ... and let him fall to the ground; a soldier's belt
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "strike him to the ground" means and what kind of belt it was.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 115 grammes d’argent|dix sicles d’argent}}
decisions.reason: Metric by default in French (10 shekels of 11.5 g), as the French Pentateuch; the alternative keeps the shekels. Literal keeps the original unit.

decisions.choice: unos 115 gramos de plata (default); diez siclos de plata (alternative)
decisions.reason: As the English units span, in metric at the terms note's 11.5 g a shekel; Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: kama gramu 115 za fedha (default); shekeli kumi za fedha (alternative)
decisions.reason: Metric instead of the English ounces: ten shekels at 11.5 g is about 115 g, as the terms notes reckon it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ אֶל־יוֹאָ֔ב וְל֨וּאאָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁקֵ֤ל עַל־כַּפַּי֙ אֶ֣לֶף כֶּ֔סֶף לֹֽא־אֶשְׁלַ֥ח יָדִ֖י אֶל־בֶּן־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י בְאָזְנֵ֜ינוּ צִוָּ֣ה הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֹ֠תְךָ וְאֶת־אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שִׁמְרוּ־מִ֕י בַּנַּ֖עַר בְּאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the man to Joab, And if I [were] weighing on my palms a thousand [of] silver, not would I stretch out my hand against [the] son of the king; for in our ears commanded the king you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Guard, whoever, the young man, Absalom.

en.L: And the man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing 1,000 [shekels of] silver on my palms, I would not stretch out my hand against the king's son. For in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Guard, whoever [you are], the young man Absalom.'
en.B: But the man answered Joab, "Even if I felt the weight of {{units:about 25 pounds of silver|a thousand shekels of silver}} in my hands, I would not raise my hand against the king's son. We all heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Whoever you are, keep the young man Absalom safe.'
en.R: But the man answered Joab, "Even if someone put {{units:about 25 pounds of silver|a thousand shekels of silver}} in my hands, I would not hurt the king's son. We all heard the king give this order to you and Abishai and Ittai: 'Whoever you are, keep young Absalom safe.'

es.L: Y el hombre dijo a Joab: «Aunque yo pesara en mis palmas mil [siclos de] plata, no extendería mi mano contra el hijo del rey. Porque a nuestros oídos el rey te mandó a ti, a Abisai y a Itai, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Guarden|Guardad}}, quienquiera [que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}}], al joven Absalón”.
es.B: Pero el hombre le respondió a Joab: «Aunque sintiera en mis manos el peso de {{units:unos 11,5 kilos de plata|mil siclos de plata}}, no levantaría la mano contra el hijo del rey. Todos oímos al rey darles esta orden a ti, a Abisai y a Itai: “Quienquiera que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}}, {{plural_you:protejan|proteged}} al joven Absalón”.
es.R: Pero el hombre le respondió a Joab: «Aunque alguien me pusiera en las manos {{units:unos 11,5 kilos de plata|mil siclos de plata}}, no le haría daño al hijo del rey. Todos oímos al rey darles esta orden a ti, a Abisai y a Itai: “Quienquiera que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}}, {{plural_you:protejan|proteged}} al joven Absalón”.

fr.L: Et l’homme dit à Joab : « Même si je pesais sur mes paumes mille [sicles d’]argent, je n’étendrais pas la main contre le fils du roi. Car à nos oreilles le roi t’a commandé, à toi, à Abishaï et à Ittaï, disant : “Gardez, qui que [vous soyez], le jeune homme Absalom.”
fr.B: Mais l’homme répondit à Joab : « Même si je sentais peser dans mes mains {{units:environ 11,5 kilos d’argent|mille sicles d’argent}}, je ne porterais pas la main sur le fils du roi. Nous avons tous entendu le roi vous ordonner, à toi, à Abishaï et à Ittaï : “Qui que vous soyez, épargnez le jeune Absalom.”
fr.R: Mais l’homme a répondu à Joab : « Même si quelqu’un me mettait {{units:environ 11,5 kilos d’argent|mille sicles d’argent}} dans les mains, je ne ferais pas de mal au fils du roi. Nous avons tous entendu le roi vous donner cet ordre, à toi, à Abishaï et à Ittaï : “Qui que vous soyez, protégez le jeune Absalom.”

sw.L: Yule mtu akamwambia Yoabu, "Hata kama ningekuwa nikipima [shekeli] 1,000 za fedha viganjani mwangu, nisingenyosha mkono wangu juu ya mwana wa mfalme. Kwa maana masikioni mwetu mfalme alikuamuru wewe na Abishai na Itai, akisema, 'Mlindeni, yeyote [mlivyo], kijana Absalomu.'
sw.B: Lakini yule mtu akamjibu Yoabu, "Hata kama ningehisi uzito wa {{units:kama kilo 11.5 za fedha|shekeli elfu moja za fedha}} mikononi mwangu, nisingeinua mkono wangu dhidi ya mwana wa mfalme. Sisi sote tulimsikia mfalme akikuamuru wewe na Abishai na Itai, 'Yeyote mlivyo, mlindeni kijana Absalomu.'
sw.R: Lakini yule mtu akamjibu Yoabu, "Hata kama mtu angeweka {{units:kama kilo 11.5 za fedha|shekeli elfu moja za fedha}} mikononi mwangu, nisingemdhuru mwana wa mfalme. Sisi sote tulimsikia mfalme akikupa amri hii wewe na Abishai na Itai: 'Yeyote mlivyo, mlindeni kijana Absalomu.'

vi.L: Người ấy nói với Giô-áp: "Dù tôi có cân 1.000 [siếc-lơ] bạc trên lòng bàn tay mình, tôi cũng không giơ tay ra hại con trai của vua. Vì chính tai chúng tôi đã nghe vua truyền lệnh cho ông, A-bi-sai và Y-tai rằng: 'Dù là ai, hãy gìn giữ chàng trai Áp-sa-lôm.'
vi.B: Nhưng người ấy đáp: "Dù có cầm trong tay {{units:khoảng 11,5 kg bạc|một nghìn siếc-lơ bạc}}, tôi cũng không dám giơ tay hại con trai của vua. Chính chúng tôi đã nghe vua truyền lệnh cho ông, A-bi-sai và Y-tai: 'Dù là ai đi nữa, hãy giữ an toàn cho chàng trai Áp-sa-lôm.'
vi.R: Nhưng người ấy trả lời Giô-áp: "Dù có ai đặt vào tay tôi {{units:khoảng 11,5 kg bạc|một nghìn siếc-lơ bạc}}, tôi cũng không làm hại con trai của vua. Tất cả chúng tôi đều đã nghe vua ra lệnh cho ông, A-bi-sai và Y-tai: 'Dù là ai đi nữa, hãy giữ an toàn cho Áp-sa-lôm trẻ tuổi.'

ko.L: 그 사람이 요압에게 말했다. "제 손바닥에 은 천 [세겔]을 달아 받는다 해도, 저는 왕의 아들에게 손을 대지 않겠습니다. 왕께서 우리가 듣는 데서 장군님과 아비새와 잇대에게 '누구든지 그 젊은이 압살롬을 지켜라' 하고 명령하셨기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 그 사람이 요압에게 대답했다. "{{units:은 11.5킬로그램쯤|은 천 세겔}}이 제 손에 쥐어진다 해도, 저는 왕의 아들에게 손을 대지 않겠습니다. 왕께서 장군님과 아비새와 잇대에게 '누구든지 젊은 압살롬을 지켜 주어라' 하고 명령하시는 것을 우리가 모두 들었습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 그 사람이 요압에게 대답했다. "누가 {{units:은 11.5킬로그램쯤|은 천 세겔}}을 제 손에 쥐여 준다 해도, 저는 왕의 아들을 해치지 않겠습니다. 왕께서 장군님과 아비새와 잇대에게 '누구든지 젊은 압살롬을 지켜 주어라' 하고 명령하시는 것을 우리가 모두 들었습니다.

decisions.choice: even if: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "and not"; the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) is "and if", which gives the sense "even if". The marked reading fits the sentence and is followed.

decisions.choice: weighing a thousand on my palms: even if the money were paid out into my hands
decisions.reason: Silver was paid by weighing it. The man answers Joab's offer of ten shekels (verse 11): not even a hundred times as much would make him do it.

decisions.choice: stretch out my hand against: attack, harm
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of not harming the Lord's anointed (1 Samuel 24:7; 26:9). The man treats the king's son with the same caution.

decisions.choice: guard, whoever you are, the young man: let every one of you protect him
alternatives: guard the young man for me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "whoever" is unusual here: the king's order covered anyone who met Absalom. A few Hebrew manuscripts and some early translations read "for me" instead ("guard the young man for me"), as in verse 5. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: about 25 pounds of silver
decisions.reason: A thousand shekels is about 25 pounds. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the shekel as the alternative.

decisions.choice: We all heard
decisions.reason: "In our ears" means that the soldiers heard it themselves (verse 5).

decisions.choice: kama kilo 11.5 za fedha (default); shekeli elfu moja za fedha (alternative)
decisions.reason: Metric instead of the English pounds: a thousand shekels at 11.5 g is about 11.5 kg.

decisions.choice: the soldier speaks to Joab in the formal style (합쇼체), calling him "장군님"; Joab answers in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: A soldier addressing the army commander; "장군님" is the ordinary Korean address for a general.

source.text: אֽוֹ־עָשִׂ֤יתִי בְנַפְשִׁי֙ שֶׁ֔קֶר וְכָל־דָּבָ֖ר לֹא־יִכָּחֵ֣ד מִן־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב מִנֶּֽגֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: Or I had done against my life falsehood, and any thing not is hidden from the king, and you, you would stand from in front.

en.L: Or [if] I had dealt falsely against my own life, and nothing is hidden from the king, then you yourself would have stood aloof."
en.B: And if I had acted treacherously and put my own life at risk, you yourself would have stood back and kept out of it, because nothing is hidden from the king."
en.R: If I had disobeyed the king and killed Absalom, I would have lost my own life. The king finds out everything. And you would not have stood up for me."

es.L: O [si] yo hubiera obrado con falsedad contra mi propia vida, pues nada se le oculta al rey, tú mismo te habrías mantenido aparte».
es.B: Y si yo hubiera actuado a traición, poniendo en peligro mi propia vida, tú mismo te habrías hecho a un lado y te habrías desentendido, porque al rey no se le oculta nada».
es.R: Si yo hubiera desobedecido al rey y hubiera matado a Absalón, habría perdido mi propia vida. El rey se entera de todo. Y tú no me habrías defendido».

fr.L: Ou [si] j’avais agi avec fausseté contre ma propre vie — et rien n’est caché au roi —, toi-même tu te serais tenu à l’écart. »
fr.B: Et si j’avais agi en traître au péril de ma vie, toi-même tu te serais tenu à l’écart, car rien n’échappe au roi. »
fr.R: Si j’avais désobéi au roi et tué Absalom, j’aurais perdu la vie. Le roi finit toujours par tout savoir. Et toi, tu ne m’aurais pas défendu. »

sw.L: Au [kama] ningetenda kwa hila juu ya uhai wangu mwenyewe, wala hakuna jambo linalofichika kwa mfalme, basi wewe mwenyewe ungesimama mbali."
sw.B: Na kama ningetenda kwa hila na kuhatarisha uhai wangu mwenyewe, wewe mwenyewe ungesimama mbali usijihusishe, kwa sababu hakuna jambo linalofichika kwa mfalme."
sw.R: Kama ningemwasi mfalme nikamwua Absalomu, ningepoteza uhai wangu mwenyewe. Mfalme hugundua kila kitu. Nawe usingenitetea."

vi.L: Hoặc [nếu] tôi đã làm điều dối trá nghịch lại mạng sống mình, mà không việc gì giấu được vua, thì chính ông cũng sẽ đứng xa."
vi.B: Còn nếu tôi phản bội mà liều mạng mình, thì chính ông cũng sẽ đứng ngoài, không can thiệp, vì không việc gì giấu được vua."
vi.R: Nếu tôi đã cãi lệnh vua mà giết Áp-sa-lôm, thì tôi đã mất mạng rồi. Vua biết hết mọi việc. Và ông cũng sẽ chẳng bênh vực tôi đâu."

ko.L: 혹시 제가 제 목숨을 걸고 거짓을 행했더라도, 왕께는 아무것도 숨길 수 없으니, 장군님께서도 [저를] 멀리하셨을 것입니다."
ko.B: 제가 왕을 배신하여 제 목숨을 위태롭게 했더라도, 장군님께서는 물러서서 모른 체하셨을 것입니다. 왕께는 아무것도 숨길 수 없기 때문입니다."
ko.R: 제가 왕의 명령을 어기고 압살롬을 죽였다면 저는 목숨을 잃었을 것입니다. 왕께서는 무엇이든지 다 알아내십니다. 그리고 장군님께서도 저를 편들어 주지 않으셨을 것입니다."

decisions.choice: against my own life: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "and my life"; the reading marked to be read aloud (qere) is "against my life", that is, at the cost of my own life. Some read the phrase as "against his life", meaning Absalom's, but that needs a change to the text. Either way the man means that killing Absalom would have been a betrayal of the king that he would have paid for himself.

decisions.choice: falsehood: an act of treachery against the king's order
decisions.reason: The word means lying or deceit. To kill Absalom after the king's public order would be to act falsely toward the king.

decisions.choice: nothing is hidden from the king: the king would find out
decisions.reason: The woman of Tekoa said the same of David's wisdom (14:20). The soldier knows that he could not hide what he had done.

decisions.choice: you would stand aloof: you would not take my side
decisions.reason: To stand "at a distance" is to keep apart from someone in trouble. The soldier expects that Joab would have left him to face the king alone.

decisions.choice: because nothing is hidden from the king
decisions.reason: Balanced moves the remark to the end, where it reads as the reason the soldier would have been found out.

decisions.choice: disobeyed the king and killed Absalom; I would have lost my own life
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the treachery would have been and what "against my life" means.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֔ב לֹא־כֵ֖ן אֹחִ֣ילָה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיִּקַּח֩ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה שְׁבָטִ֜ים בְּכַפּ֗וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֵם֙ בְּלֵ֣ב אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם עוֹדֶ֥נּוּ חַ֖י בְּלֵ֥ב הָאֵלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joab, Not thus will I wait before you. And he took three rods in his palm and thrust them into [the] heart of Absalom, still he [was] alive in [the] heart of the terebinth.

en.L: And Joab said, "Not so will I wait before you." And he took three rods in his palm and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he [was] still alive in the heart of the terebinth.
en.B: Joab said, "I will not waste any more time with you like this." He took three rods in his hand and drove them into Absalom's chest while Absalom was still alive in the middle of the tree.
en.R: Joab said, "I am not going to stand here waiting for you." He took three sticks in his hand and drove them into Absalom's chest. Absalom was still alive, hanging in the tree.

es.L: Y Joab dijo: «No me quedaré así esperando delante de ti». Y tomó tres varas en su mano y las clavó en el corazón de Absalón, estando él aún vivo en medio de la encina.
es.B: Joab dijo: «No voy a perder más tiempo contigo». Tomó tres varas en la mano y se las clavó en el pecho a Absalón mientras este todavía estaba vivo en medio del árbol.
es.R: Joab dijo: «No voy a quedarme aquí esperándote». Tomó tres palos en la mano y se los clavó en el pecho a Absalón. Absalón todavía estaba vivo, colgado del árbol.

fr.L: Et Joab dit : « Je ne m’attarderai pas ainsi devant toi. » Et il prit trois bâtons dans sa main et les enfonça dans le cœur d’Absalom, encore vivant au cœur du térébinthe.
fr.B: Joab dit : « Je ne vais pas perdre plus de temps avec toi. » Il prit trois bâtons en main et les enfonça dans la poitrine d’Absalom, qui était encore vivant au milieu de l’arbre.
fr.R: Joab a dit : « Je ne vais pas rester ici à t’attendre. » Il a pris trois bâtons dans sa main et les a enfoncés dans la poitrine d’Absalom. Absalom était encore vivant, pendu dans l’arbre.

sw.L: Yoabu akasema, "Sitangoja hivi mbele yako." Akachukua fimbo tatu mkononi mwake akazichoma ndani ya moyo wa Absalomu, alipokuwa bado hai katikati ya mwaloni.
sw.B: Yoabu akasema, "Sitapoteza muda zaidi nawe hivi." Akachukua fimbo tatu mkononi mwake, akazichoma ndani ya kifua cha Absalomu, alipokuwa bado hai katikati ya mti.
sw.R: Yoabu akasema, "Sitasimama hapa kukusubiri." Akachukua vijiti vitatu mkononi mwake, akavichoma ndani ya kifua cha Absalomu. Absalomu alikuwa bado hai, akining'inia mtini.

vi.L: Giô-áp nói: "Ta không chờ trước mặt ngươi như thế này nữa." Ông lấy ba cây gậy trong tay và đâm vào tim Áp-sa-lôm, trong khi chàng [còn] sống giữa lòng cây sồi.
vi.B: Giô-áp nói: "Ta không phí thời giờ với ngươi như thế này nữa." Ông cầm ba cây gậy trong tay và đâm vào ngực Áp-sa-lôm trong khi chàng còn sống, đang bị treo giữa cây sồi.
vi.R: Giô-áp nói: "Ta không đứng đây chờ ngươi nữa." Ông cầm ba cây gậy trong tay và đâm vào ngực Áp-sa-lôm. Lúc ấy Áp-sa-lôm vẫn còn sống, đang bị treo trên cây.

ko.L: 요압이 말했다. "내가 이렇게 네 앞에서 머뭇거리고 있지 않겠다." 그리고 그는 손에 막대기 세 개를 들고 가서, 아직 테레빈나무 한가운데에 산 채로 [매달려] 있는 압살롬의 심장을 찔렀다.
ko.B: 요압이 말했다. "너와 이렇게 시간을 낭비하지 않겠다." 그는 손에 막대기 세 개를 들고 가서, 아직 나무 한가운데에 산 채로 매달려 있는 압살롬의 가슴을 찔렀다.
ko.R: 요압이 말했다. "너를 기다리며 여기 서 있지 않겠다." 요압은 손에 막대기 세 개를 들고 가서 압살롬의 가슴을 찔렀다. 압살롬은 아직 살아서 나무에 매달려 있었다.

decisions.choice: rods: sticks or clubs, perhaps pointed
decisions.reason: The word usually means a rod, staff or club. The ancient Greek translation reads "darts". Joab's blows do not kill Absalom at once; his armor-bearers finish him (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the heart of Absalom ... the heart of the terebinth: his chest, in the middle of the tree
decisions.reason: "Heart" is used twice: of Absalom's body and of the middle of the tree. The repeated word ties the man and the tree together.

decisions.choice: not so will I wait before you: I will not stand here arguing
decisions.reason: Joab cuts the conversation short and acts himself.

decisions.choice: Absalom's chest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "chest" for the first "heart", since Absalom was not killed at once; Literal keeps the repeated word.

decisions.choice: sticks
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for rods.

source.text: וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֣י יוֹאָ֑ב וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם וַיְמִיתֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And surrounded ten young men, bearers of [the] weapons of Joab, and struck Absalom and killed him.

en.L: And ten young men, bearers of Joab's weapons, surrounded [him] and struck Absalom and killed him.
en.B: Then ten young men, Joab's armor-bearers, closed in around Absalom, struck him down and killed him.
en.R: Then ten young men who carried Joab's weapons for him gathered around Absalom. They attacked him and killed him.

es.L: Y diez jóvenes, escuderos de Joab, [lo] rodearon e hirieron a Absalón y lo mataron.
es.B: Entonces diez jóvenes, los escuderos de Joab, rodearon a Absalón, lo hirieron y lo mataron.
es.R: Entonces diez jóvenes que le llevaban las armas a Joab rodearon a Absalón. Lo atacaron y lo mataron.

fr.L: Et dix jeunes gens, porteurs des armes de Joab, [l’]entourèrent, et frappèrent Absalom et le tuèrent.
fr.B: Puis dix jeunes gens, les écuyers de Joab, entourèrent Absalom, le frappèrent et l’achevèrent.
fr.R: Ensuite, dix jeunes hommes qui portaient les armes de Joab se sont mis autour d’Absalom. Ils l’ont frappé et l’ont tué.

sw.L: Vijana kumi, wabeba silaha za Yoabu, wakamzunguka, wakampiga Absalomu, wakamwua.
sw.B: Kisha vijana kumi, wabeba silaha wa Yoabu, wakamzunguka Absalomu, wakampiga na kumwua.
sw.R: Kisha vijana kumi waliombebea Yoabu silaha zake wakamzunguka Absalomu. Wakamshambulia, wakamwua.

vi.L: Mười thanh niên mang vũ khí của Giô-áp vây quanh, đánh Áp-sa-lôm và giết chàng.
vi.B: Bấy giờ mười thanh niên mang khí giới cho Giô-áp vây quanh Áp-sa-lôm, đánh chàng và giết chết.
vi.R: Rồi mười thanh niên mang vũ khí cho Giô-áp vây quanh Áp-sa-lôm. Họ tấn công và giết chết chàng.

ko.L: 요압의 무기를 든 젊은이 열 명이 [그를] 둘러싸고 압살롬을 쳐서 죽였다.
ko.B: 그러자 요압의 무기를 드는 젊은이 열 명이 압살롬을 에워싸고 그를 쳐 죽였다.
ko.R: 그러자 요압의 무기를 들고 다니던 젊은이 열 명이 압살롬을 둘러쌌다. 그들은 압살롬을 공격하여 죽였다.

decisions.choice: bearers of Joab's weapons: his armor-bearers
decisions.reason: An armor-bearer carried a warrior's weapons and fought at his side (1 Samuel 14:6-14; 31:4-5). Ten of them show Joab's high rank.

decisions.choice: struck and killed him: they finished him off
decisions.reason: Joab wounded Absalom; his men gave the blows that killed him.

decisions.choice: Joab's armor-bearers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "bearers of the weapons" is the usual English "armor-bearers"; Literal keeps the longer phrase.

source.text: וַיִּתְקַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ בַּשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַיָּ֣שָׁב הָעָ֔ם מִרְדֹ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־חָשַׂ֥ךְ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And blew Joab on the trumpet, and turned back the people from pursuing after Israel, for held back Joab the people.

en.L: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people turned back from pursuing after Israel, for Joab held back the people.
en.B: Then Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops turned back from chasing Israel, because Joab held the army back.
en.R: Then Joab blew the ram's horn, and his soldiers stopped chasing the men of Israel. Joab held them back.

es.L: Y Joab tocó la trompeta, y el pueblo dejó de perseguir a Israel, porque Joab detuvo al pueblo.
es.B: Entonces Joab tocó la trompeta, y la tropa dejó de perseguir a Israel, porque Joab contuvo al ejército.
es.R: Entonces Joab tocó el cuerno de carnero, y sus soldados dejaron de perseguir a los hombres de Israel. Joab los detuvo.

fr.L: Et Joab sonna de la trompette, et le peuple revint de la poursuite d’Israël, car Joab retint le peuple.
fr.B: Alors Joab sonna de la trompette, et la troupe cessa de poursuivre Israël, car Joab retint l’armée.
fr.R: Alors Joab a sonné de la corne de bélier, et ses soldats ont arrêté de poursuivre les hommes d’Israël. Joab les a retenus.

sw.L: Yoabu akapiga tarumbeta, na watu wakarudi kutoka kuwafuatia Israeli, kwa maana Yoabu aliwazuia watu.
sw.B: Ndipo Yoabu akapiga tarumbeta, na askari wakarudi wasiendelee kuwafuatia Israeli, kwa sababu Yoabu alilizuia jeshi.
sw.R: Ndipo Yoabu akapiga pembe ya kondoo dume, na askari wake wakaacha kuwafukuza watu wa Israeli. Yoabu akawazuia.

vi.L: Giô-áp thổi kèn, và dân quay về, thôi đuổi theo Y-sơ-ra-ên, vì Giô-áp cầm dân lại.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Giô-áp thổi kèn, và quân lính thôi đuổi theo Y-sơ-ra-ên mà quay về, vì Giô-áp giữ quân lại.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Giô-áp thổi tù và, và binh sĩ thôi đuổi theo quân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Giô-áp cầm quân lại.

ko.L: 요압이 나팔을 불자, 백성이 이스라엘을 뒤쫓다가 돌아왔다. 요압이 백성을 말렸기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러자 요압이 나팔을 불었고, 군대는 이스라엘을 뒤쫓다가 돌아왔다. 요압이 군대를 붙들었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러자 요압이 숫양 뿔나팔을 불었다. 그러자 군사들은 이스라엘 사람들을 뒤쫓다가 멈추었다. 요압이 그들을 멈추게 한 것이다.

decisions.choice: trumpet: a ram's horn, blown as a signal in war
decisions.reason: As in 2:28, the shofar tells the army to stop fighting.

decisions.choice: for Joab held back the people: he stopped the killing
decisions.reason: With Absalom dead the revolt was over, and the men fleeing were David's own people. The text does not give Joab's reason, but compare 2:26-28, where Joab also stops a pursuit of fellow Israelites.

decisions.choice: the troops, the army (Balanced); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army" or "the soldiers".

decisions.choice: the ram's horn
decisions.reason: Readable names the instrument itself, as in 2:28.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וַיַּשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אֹת֤וֹ בַיַּ֨עַר֙ אֶל־הַפַּ֣חַת הַגָּד֔וֹל וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ עָלָ֛יו גַּל־אֲבָנִ֖ים גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֑ד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they took Absalom and threw him in the forest into the pit, the great [one], and set up over him a heap of stones very great; and all Israel fled, each to his tents.

en.L: And they took Absalom and threw him into the great pit in the forest, and they set up over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his tent.
en.B: They took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest, then raised a huge heap of stones over him. And all Israel fled, every man to his home.
en.R: They took Absalom's body and threw it into a big hole in the forest. Then they piled a huge heap of stones on top of it. All the men of Israel ran away to their homes.

es.L: Y tomaron a Absalón y lo echaron en el gran hoyo en el bosque, y levantaron sobre él un montón de piedras muy grande. Y todo Israel huyó, cada uno a su tienda.
es.B: Tomaron a Absalón, lo arrojaron a un gran hoyo en el bosque y levantaron sobre él un enorme montón de piedras. Y todo Israel huyó, cada uno a su casa.
es.R: Tomaron el cuerpo de Absalón y lo echaron en un hoyo grande en el bosque. Luego amontonaron encima una enorme pila de piedras. Todos los hombres de Israel huyeron a sus casas.

fr.L: Et ils prirent Absalom et le jetèrent dans la grande fosse, dans la forêt, et ils élevèrent sur lui un très grand monceau de pierres. Et tout Israël s’enfuit, chacun à sa tente.
fr.B: On prit Absalom et on le jeta dans une grande fosse, dans la forêt, puis on dressa sur lui un énorme tas de pierres. Et tout Israël s’enfuit, chacun chez soi.
fr.R: Ils ont pris le corps d’Absalom et l’ont jeté dans un grand trou, dans la forêt. Puis ils ont empilé dessus un énorme tas de pierres. Tous les hommes d’Israël se sont enfuis chez eux.

sw.L: Wakamchukua Absalomu wakamtupa katika shimo kubwa msituni, wakasimamisha juu yake rundo kubwa sana la mawe. Na Israeli wote wakakimbia, kila mtu hemani kwake.
sw.B: Wakamchukua Absalomu wakamtupa katika shimo kubwa msituni, kisha wakarundika juu yake chungu kubwa mno la mawe. Na Israeli wote wakakimbia, kila mtu nyumbani kwake.
sw.R: Wakauchukua mwili wa Absalomu wakautupa katika shimo kubwa msituni. Kisha wakarundika juu yake chungu kubwa sana la mawe. Watu wote wa Israeli wakakimbilia nyumbani kwao.

vi.L: Họ lấy Áp-sa-lôm ném vào cái hố lớn trong rừng, rồi chất trên chàng một đống đá rất lớn. Còn cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đều chạy trốn, ai về trại nấy.
vi.B: Họ đem Áp-sa-lôm ném xuống một cái hố lớn trong rừng, rồi chất lên trên một đống đá thật lớn. Còn cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đều chạy trốn, ai về nhà nấy.
vi.R: Họ lấy xác Áp-sa-lôm ném xuống một cái hố lớn trong rừng. Rồi họ chất một đống đá rất lớn lên trên. Tất cả quân Y-sơ-ra-ên đều chạy trốn về nhà mình.

ko.L: 그들이 압살롬을 가져다가 숲속의 큰 구덩이에 던지고, 그 위에 매우 큰 돌무더기를 쌓았다. 온 이스라엘은 저마다 자기 장막으로 도망쳤다.
ko.B: 사람들은 압살롬을 가져다가 숲속의 큰 구덩이에 던지고, 그 위에 아주 큰 돌무더기를 쌓아 올렸다. 그리고 온 이스라엘은 저마다 자기 집으로 도망쳤다.
ko.R: 사람들은 압살롬의 시체를 가져다가 숲속의 큰 구덩이에 던졌다. 그리고 그 위에 아주 큰 돌무더기를 쌓았다. 이스라엘 사람들은 모두 자기 집으로 달아났다.

decisions.choice: a heap of stones over him: the burial of a man under a curse
decisions.reason: A heap of stones was raised over Achan and over the king of Ai (Joshua 7:26; 8:29). Absalom gets no family tomb, only a pit in the forest; the next verse sets this beside the pillar he had built for himself.

decisions.choice: each to his tent: each man to his home
decisions.reason: "To your tents" is an old way of saying "go home" (20:1; 1 Kings 12:16). Absalom's army broke up and went home.

decisions.choice: his tent: written and marked readings agree in sense
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "his tent"; the reading marked to be read aloud (qere) is "his tents". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: every man to his home (Balanced); to their homes (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom.

decisions.choice: Absalom's body
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Absalom was already dead.

source.text: וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֣ם לָקַ֗ח וַיַּצֶּב־ל֤וֹ בְחַיָּיו֙ אֶת־מַצֶּ֨בֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעֵֽמֶק־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֤י אָמַר֙ אֵֽין־לִ֣י בֵ֔ן בַּעֲב֖וּר הַזְכִּ֣יר שְׁמִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לַמַּצֶּ֨בֶת֙ עַל־שְׁמ֔וֹ וַיִּקָּ֤רֵא לָהּ֙ יַ֣ד אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And Absalom had taken and set up for himself in his life the pillar which [is] in [the] Valley of the King, for he said, There is not to me a son in order to cause to remember my name; and he called the pillar by his name, and it is called Monument of Absalom until this day.

en.L: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself the pillar that [is] in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name remembered." And he called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.
en.B: During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and set it up for himself in the King's Valley, because he said, "I have no son to keep my name remembered." He named the pillar after himself, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.
en.R: While Absalom was still alive, he had set up a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley. He said, "I have no son to keep people remembering my name." So he named the pillar after himself. It is called Absalom's Monument to this day.

es.L: Y Absalón, en vida, había tomado y levantado para sí la columna que [está] en el valle del Rey, porque dijo: «No tengo hijo que haga recordar mi nombre». Y llamó a la columna por su propio nombre, y se llama el Monumento de Absalón hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Mientras vivía, Absalón había tomado una columna y la había levantado para sí en el valle del Rey, porque decía: «No tengo ningún hijo que haga recordar mi nombre». Le puso a la columna su propio nombre, y hasta el día de hoy se llama el Monumento de Absalón.
es.R: Cuando Absalón todavía vivía, se había levantado una columna de piedra en el valle del Rey. Había dicho: «No tengo ningún hijo que haga que la gente recuerde mi nombre». Así que le puso a la columna su propio nombre. Hasta el día de hoy se llama el Monumento de Absalón.

fr.L: Or Absalom avait pris et dressé pour lui-même, de son vivant, la stèle qui [est] dans la vallée du Roi, car il disait : « Je n’ai pas de fils pour faire rappeler mon nom. » Et il appela la stèle de son propre nom, et on l’appelle le Monument d’Absalom jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: De son vivant, Absalom avait pris une stèle et l’avait dressée pour lui-même dans la vallée du Roi, car il disait : « Je n’ai pas de fils pour garder vivant le souvenir de mon nom. » Il donna son propre nom à la stèle, et on l’appelle aujourd’hui encore le Monument d’Absalom.
fr.R: Quand il était encore vivant, Absalom avait dressé pour lui-même une colonne de pierre dans la vallée du Roi. Il disait : « Je n’ai pas de fils pour que les gens se souviennent de mon nom. » Il a donc donné son nom à cette colonne. On l’appelle encore aujourd’hui le Monument d’Absalom.
